tonight.headline: Jefferson and Addison come down to a pregame workout; you trail 31.5 to nothing
body: Bad news first. Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, both questionable, 'will work out pregame to determine their status'. Nobody with access has said either is expected to play, and your fallback for one is the other. Kyle Monangai is out with nothing new on how long. You are 0–4 and 31.5 behind on Bucky Irving's Thursday night; ESPN has it 125.2 to 130.8 and gives you 47%.

Better news around them: Alvin Kamara is expected to play, Terry McLaurin carries a 'slight lean' toward playing, and Adam Schefter says Rico Dowdle is unlikely to, which ESPN has already put into Jaylen Warren's number, up from 14.5 to 17.7. This brief is written at 07:30, two hours before the inactive lists. Everything below that rests on a questionable tag is provisional. At 09:30 read four names, Jefferson, Addison, McLaurin and Kamara, and fire the two cards from the list.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Irving's 31.5 is banked (archive). Ja'Marr Chase, 21.8, is still on their bench and still questionable: no report of a concussion clearance had been published by 06:47 ET (SI Betting), and Cincinnati elevated no receiver on Saturday night, which The Athletic's Paul Dehner Jr. reads as leaving the door open for Chase and Tee Higgins to play. Kendre Miller, 7.9, is in their flex, and Kamara playing takes work from him. If Chase is cleared and they start him, their 130.8 rises by about fourteen. Trey McBride's quarterback is without Marvin Harrison Jr., who is inactive with a trade pending.

case.label: Your side
case.body: As set: Allen 20.1, Jefferson 18.6, Warren 17.7, Wilson 14.7, Tuten 14.0, Likely 12.9, Gordon 10.9, Fairbairn 8.5, the Vikings 7.8. Warren's number rose 3.2 since Saturday because ESPN now projects Dowdle at 0.0. Tuten kicked off in London at 07:30, after this snapshot.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The 09:30 inactive lists: Jefferson, Addison, McLaurin and Kamara on your side, Chase on theirs. Nothing published this morning settles the Vikings pair.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · provisional until the inactive list · check Sun 09:30 Mexico City · kickoff 11:00
doFirst.title: 09:30: if Jefferson is inactive, Addison; if both, McLaurin
doFirst.subtitle: Rapoport, Sunday morning: both Vikings receivers work out before the game and Minnesota decide then. Do nothing until the inactive list; the order is set here so 09:30 is a checklist.

case.label: Where it stands
case.body: Ian Rapoport, Sunday morning: Jefferson (ankle) and Addison (hamstring) 'are both questionable and will work out pregame to determine their status' (The Big Lead relaying his post, 11 Oct 07:47 ET; NBC Sports, 08:32 ET: both 'remain game-time decisions'). He adds that Jefferson has said he will do whatever he can to play in a Louisiana homecoming game. No insider has said either is expected to play, and none has said either is not. Minnesota elevated Odell Beckham Jr. and Jeshaun Jones on Saturday.

case.label: The order
case.body: Jefferson, 18.6, starts if he is active: 7.2 above Addison is not a coin flip. If he is inactive, Addison, 11.4, takes the slot if active. If both are inactive, McLaurin, 12.8, takes the receiver slot if he is active and Gordon stays in the flex. All of them kick off at 11:00.

case.label: If all three sit
case.body: Then the free add is Romeo Doubs, 12.2, for Monangai, who is out. New England play at 11:00 too. Mack Hollins is on injured reserve; A.J. Brown has not been activated.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Jefferson is active and Addison outscores him today (archive). If Jefferson is inactive this card fires and the open lineup thesis closes untested.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · fire it from the inactive list, Sun 09:30 Mexico City · both kick off Sun 11:00
doFirst.title: 09:30: McLaurin into the flex if he is active
doFirst.subtitle: ESPN's John Keim on Saturday: still a game-time decision, with a 'slight lean' toward playing. 12.8 against Gordon's 10.9 is a coin flip, and coin flips go to the projection. Wait for the list.

case.label: What the check says
case.body: As set you project 125.2; the projection lineup is 127.1. The whole 1.9 is McLaurin over Gordon in the flex, and the tool labels it COIN FLIP. The rule for a coin flip is to take the projection and write nothing more.

case.label: What the reports say
case.body: One limited practice, on Friday, after a missed game. John Keim of ESPN, on Saturday: a game-time decision with a 'slight lean' toward playing (via RotoWire, 10 Oct; the hour is not shown). He is not in NFL.com's Sunday-morning tracker, so there is no Sunday word. Stefon Diggs is out and Jayden Daniels starts. Three forecasts read this morning have light rain or drizzle at Landover and wind of 8 to 12 mph, milder than Saturday's brief said.

case.label: If he is inactive
case.body: The tool's fallback is Kamara, 11.2, who is expected to play; that is 0.3 over Gordon, 10.9, a coin flip. Take Kamara only if he is on the active side of the same 09:30 list; otherwise Gordon stays where he is.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McLaurin starts in your flex and Gordon outscores him today (archive). No thesis rides on it either way: it is a coin flip.

whatWentWrong.title: Both Vikings receivers are a pregame workout, and each is the other's cover
whatWentWrong.lead: Rapoport this morning: both work out before the game. Nobody has reported that either is expected to play.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Jefferson limited three days, Addison two; both questionable. Rapoport on Sunday morning has both working out pregame with the decision made from how they look (NFL.com tracker; RotoWire, 11 Oct). No lean from Schefter, Pelissero, Fowler, Seifert or the Star Tribune was found. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is out.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The first card's order: Addison first, McLaurin second, and the reason McLaurin's own status matters twice.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The inactive list at 09:30 Mexico City. This brief is written before it and cannot see it.

whatWentWrong.title: Monangai is out, in a boot, with no return date
whatWentWrong.lead: Nothing new since Friday. His is the seat Tuesday's claims would use.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Out for Green Bay with turf toe, in a walking boot after seeing a specialist, week-to-week and not headed for injured reserve (Patrick Finley, Sun-Times, 9 Oct). No Sunday item on him was found. D'Andre Swift has no designation; Caleb Williams is not expected to play (Mike Garafolo, 11 Oct), so Tyson Bagent starts.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: No lineup move: he is on your bench at 0.0. It matters for the first card's last resort and for Tuesday, when Diggs clears waivers and you also need a defence for Minnesota's bye.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A return to practice on Wednesday keeps him. A second missed game or a move to injured reserve makes him the drop.

worthALook.name: Romeo Doubs
worthALook.lead: Free. Hollins is on injured reserve, so the vacancy is at least four games long, and New England have not decided whether A.J. Brown practises next week. The seat he would take is Monangai's.

case.label: The role
case.body: Mack Hollins (calf) went on injured reserve on Saturday, out at least four games (patriots.com, 10 Oct). In the game Hollins left, Doubs drew 9 targets and scored twice, 23.8 (archive); targets 3, 4, 4, 9. One writer now calls him New England's clear first receiver; the team's own site listed four receivers sharing the work. Las Vegas are without receiver Jalen Nailor, and Ashton Jeanty is hopeful but not certain to play (Rapoport, 11 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 12.2, behind McLaurin's 12.8 and only 1.3 above Gordon, so he does not clearly start this week. A.J. Brown 'continues to progress' and could return 'sooner than later', but New England have not decided whether he practises next week (Tom Pelissero, relayed by Bleacher Report, 10 Oct; that page gets two other details wrong, so treat it with care).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Monangai missing Week 6 makes this Tuesday's decision alongside Diggs; or Jefferson, Addison and McLaurin all inactive at 09:30, which makes him a starter this morning. He is a free agent, so waiting costs no priority, only the risk that a rival adds him.

case.body: 0.0 this week and nobody has said when he is back; no report mentions injured reserve either way. Remove the two-touchdown game and he has scored 7.3 and 8.5. He would be your sixth receiver, and the only seat is Monangai's.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday afternoon. Claims run at 01:00 Mexico City on Wednesday, and in this league the order resets every week, so a claim costs nothing lasting. If Monangai is still in a boot and Diggs has a practice target for Week 6, when Jefferson, Addison and Gordon are all on bye, this becomes a card.

Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quad) are out. RotoWire expects Harris to be the top target, with Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Derius Davis and Theo Wease behind him. Touches 7 and 5 for 13.6 and 9.0 in Weeks 3 and 4 (wire screen).

case.body: 9.8, below every receiver you own who plays today, and 7% rostered. It is one game of vacancy until someone says how long McConkey is out. The Chargers play at 14:25, so the result is known before Tuesday. Off in Week 7.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets against Denver and McConkey ruled out for Week 6, when Jefferson and Addison are on bye. He is a free agent; nothing is lost by reading it on Tuesday.

doNotChase.name: Roman Wilson
doNotChase.lead: Pittman went on injured reserve on Saturday, out at least four games. Wilson's targets did not move the last time he was missing.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Pittsburgh put Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve on Saturday; the earliest he can return is Week 10 (Steelers Depot, 10 Oct 15:52 ET). Heavy expects Wilson and Germie Bernard to take his snaps and targets; that is a writer's read and no coach has said it. 14 catches for 188 yards and two touchdowns so far.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Six targets in every one of his four games, the Week 2 game without Pittman included (archive). 10.2, below McLaurin and Addison on your bench, with showers certain in Pittsburgh and gusts to 26 mph (National Weather Service, 11 Oct 00:36 EDT).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets against Indianapolis. With Pittman gone for a month that would be a role and not a spike, and it would put him beside Diggs and Doubs on Tuesday's list. He is a free agent.
